doc.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022

chapter: Patti Smith and Return to Forever recordings
title: Leprechaun with Chick Corea and Steve Gadd
summary: Starting the album in December 1975, their quick rapport, the overdub approach, and no click track with Gadd.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: So then comes “Leprechaun” is that right?

Just after that is the “Leprechaun.” Now we’re talking from October to December. So I did that album and then started the “Leprechaun” in December of that year, ’75. Late ’75. And that was another major shift in influence and path of my life, going into that and working with Chick. And we hit it off really — I didn’t really get to know him much during the previous recording, I just did my job and that sort of thing. But now we were working together on a longer basis and I got to know him and we did this project together and it just fit like a glove. I knew exactly what he wanted to hear. Because I was hearing it myself. It was just easy communication.
Could you be more maybe specific about what he wanted to hear and what you heard also?

Well I mean he would play, you know, there are two types of things that were going on. There was a roomful of musicians which is one scenario. And they would be building a song, which was another scenario, which would be an overdubbing scenario where he would use synths and percussion and that sort of thing. The opening piece of that is like that. There’s just — it’s just creative fun, it’s just sounds and music. And when I heard it there was nothing to do except to make things in relationship to others in terms of volume

and panning and treatment other than what I wanted to hear, and what I wanted to hear from the different parts that were coming in were things that he agreed with. So there was that kind of reality that went on and that really continued for the course of the project.
Did they record most of that music with a click track?
Not at all. That was Steve Gadd.
So they had a click track. All right.

I mean that album, if you could, there are three components that go through that album. One is Chick, one is Steve Gadd, and the other is Gayle Moran, her vocals, all the way through. But in terms of the basic track, not the vocals of course which added so much, but just the instrumentation. There’s a lot going on but basically Chick and Steve are the — it’s almost like a duet album in a sense. If you listen to that relationship it’s just amazing for that. So there was no click track, no.
And I’ll tell you, when you deal with Chick and you deal with Steve you don’t need any click.
